questions.q: If an attacker took one server today, how many others could it reach?
questions.why: Lateral movement is how one compromised machine becomes a breach.
questions.need: The reach of one compromised server is known, and limited to what its application needs
questions.how: Map what one critical server can reach today and agree what it should reach

questions.q: Which audit or regulation asks you to separate environments, and how do you prove it today?
questions.why: Evidence for auditors turns a security wish into a budget line.
questions.need: The separation required by audit is known, with the evidence it needs
questions.how: List the requirements and the evidence each auditor expects

questions.q: Can you see which machines talk to which inside the data centre?
questions.why: Policies cannot be written for traffic nobody can see.
questions.need: East-west traffic is visible for every environment in scope
questions.how: Turn on traffic visibility, without enforcing anything, for each environment

questions.q: Are machines labelled by application, environment and role, or only known by their address?
questions.why: Policies written on addresses break when machines move; policies on labels follow them.
questions.need: Machines carry labels that policies can use, kept up to date by their owners
questions.how: Agree a labelling scheme and label the applications in scope

questions.q: Are test and production kept apart, or only on different address ranges?
questions.why: Address ranges are not a control; an isolation policy is.
questions.need: Environments are isolated by policy, and the isolation is tested
questions.how: Write isolation policies between environments and test a blocked connection

questions.q: Could you isolate a machine suspected of compromise in a minute, and still investigate it?
questions.why: Containment time decides how far an attacker gets.
questions.need: A suspect machine can be quarantined in one step, with forensic access kept
questions.how: Prepare quarantine policies and rehearse one on a test machine

questions.q: Do security policies follow a machine when it moves or fails over to another site?
questions.why: A recovery site without the same policies is an open door during the worst day.
questions.need: Policies follow workloads across hosts, sites and failover
questions.how: Test a policy before and after a migration and a failover

questions.q: Who decides on a blocked connection that an application needs, and how quickly?
questions.why: Enforcement without an owner turns into exceptions nobody reviews.
questions.need: A named owner reviews blocked connections and exceptions, with a response time
questions.how: Name the owner and agree how requests for new flows are handled
